precepts.text: Thou knowest not what is the way of the spirit, nor how the bones do grow in the womb; thou knowest not the works of God who maketh all. Science explains what God allows, then tries to outdo him by altering the body.
precepts.point: Pride is hateful before God and man. You can repent and hop back to the right side, but on the side of pride you are on the side God hates, and everything he hates has an expiration date.
precepts.why:
“As thou knowest not what is the way of the spirit”: you don't know how the spirit was even made, and the body doesn't function without a spirit in it. We say someone is soulless, and it may be jacked up and crooked like the Esau in them, but that body isn't walking around with nothing in it. This is not a movie where they clone you and you come back with no soul, or a vampire who lives forever and can't see his reflection. There is a spirit in all of us, and the Most High made that.

“nor how the bones do grow in the womb of her that is with child”. Science tries to explain it the best way it can, by the mitochondria and this and that, but they don't know what God did to make it. Science is God giving man some sense of his mastery, and man takes it and says, I can do better than God: let me put this rod on you as a woman, let me cut yours off. That's why the Bible warns us to beware of science that opposes God.

“even so thou knowest not the works of God who maketh all.” So why is earth and ashes proud? Man does not even know how he himself was made; pride was not made for men.

points: Cast your bread upon the waters, for you shall find it after many days; give a portion to seven and also to eight, for you know not what evil shall be upon the earth.

note.label: Ecclesiastes 11: Cast Thy Bread Upon the Waters

points: When the clouds are full of rain they empty themselves on the earth, and where the tree falls it stays. He that watches the wind will not sow, and he that regards the clouds will not reap; endless caution never acts.

note.label: Ecclesiastes 11: Cast Thy Bread Upon the Waters

points: As you do not know the way of the spirit nor how the bones grow in the womb of her that is with child, so you know not the works of the Most High who makes all things.

note.label: Ecclesiastes 11: Cast Thy Bread Upon the Waters

points: Sow your seed in the morning and in the evening withhold not your hand, for you do not know which shall prosper, this or that, or whether both shall be alike good. The light is sweet, and it is pleasant for the eyes to behold the sun.

note.label: Ecclesiastes 11: Cast Thy Bread Upon the Waters

points: If a man lives many years, let him rejoice in them all, yet remember the days of darkness, for they shall be many; all that comes is vanity.

note.label: Ecclesiastes 11: Cast Thy Bread Upon the Waters

points: Rejoice, young man, in your youth and walk in the ways of your heart, but know that for all these things the Most High will bring you into judgment. Remove sorrow from your heart and put away evil from your flesh, for childhood and youth are vanity.

note.label: Ecclesiastes 11: Cast Thy Bread Upon the Waters

points: “Rejoice, O young man, in thy youth”. “and walk in the ways of thine heart, and in the sight of thine eyes”. Are you supposed to walk your own heart's way? If that's what you want, walk however you want. “but know thou, that for all these things God will bring thee into judgment.” Young men think they're invincible with all their lives ahead. Live it up if you want; God will judge you. Decide whether to stay in sin, be seduced, love the world and evil rap music.
If you're different here than somewhere else, you're the devil, doing wrong. You should talk the same around anyone without being unnerved. A secret life means you're a sinner with the devil on you.

“Therefore remove sorrow from thy heart, and put away evil from thy flesh”. “for childhood and youth are vanity.” Youth is fleeting, short like a vapor. If God spares you, one day you'll wake up with gray hair. Gather wisdom and righteous memories now, so you can tell the Father you fought a good fight, kept the faith and taught his people. Or do it your way and say good morning, welcome to Walmart.
